plotSections.title: An oversized door in the woods
bullets: Gerk opens a door about eighteen feet by seven feet. A disturbance of birds marks the far end roughly a quarter mile south in the same forest.
Branches that intersect the doorway hang in a semi-translucent limbo. Gerk can feel the far end of the door he opened.
The door is much taller than his usual doors. Sylan suspects a stronger opening makes a larger door, and that this one is big enough for Glimmen.

Sylan and Ciri walk the quarter mile south instead of stepping through, in case the opening did damage. The far side is an eighteen-foot door reaching into the canopy, with intersecting branches translucent and no crater or other destruction.

They return through the portal. Sylan still does not know what made the racket, and he suggests Gerk may need to remember a place fondly to open closer to it. Gerk does not know how near to himself he can place a door.

plotSections.title: Two doors and a vacuum
bullets: Gerk tries a normal, non-rage opening aimed at a point about twenty-five feet away, across a crossing and past the lantern, after Sylan calls for Guidance. He rolls a 9.
The door opens short of the chosen spot, over the lantern, and is again about eighteen feet tall. The first door is still open.
Wind rushes between the two doors. The lantern is pulled through the new door and into the far eighteen-foot door as a vortex forms. Gerk shuts both doors and the wind dies.
To the south, branches and limbs crash to the ground.

plotSections.title: Closing the door cuts
bullets: Where branches had passed through the doorway, they are cleanly severed, with no burn marks and no leftover debris, as if sliced by a blade. The fallen limbs lie in a pile. Sylan's lantern is dinged and disheveled from being sucked through, but not shattered.

Sylan and Gerk treat the effect as extremely dangerous: a closing door could cut a creature, a rope bridge, or anyone at a destination. They agree not to use it in a crowded place. Gerk recalls Carlkin telling them to practice in the middle of a field.

They note they were lucky the earlier opening into the kitchen did not cut Mahali, and that opening onto people is a serious risk. Sylan's next idea is to try a place Gerk has already been, on the theory that a recent visit may make it easier.

chronologicalEvents: Gerk opens an eighteen-by-seven-foot door; birds disturb the forest about a quarter mile south, and branches intersecting the doorway turn semi-translucent.
Gerk feels the far end of the open door. Sylan and a hidden Ciri walk south to inspect it rather than pass through.
They find the far door reaching into the canopy, with translucent branches and no crater, then return through the portal.
Gerk attempts a normal line-of-sight opening about twenty-five feet away, past the lantern, and rolls a 9. The door opens short, over the lantern.
With the first door still open, wind and a vacuum pull the lantern from one door into the other. Gerk closes both, and branches crash to the south.
Sylan finds the intersecting limbs cleanly cut, gathers the dinged lantern, and warns Gerk that closing a door can slice whatever it intersects.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian, Doorman, and Child of the Tree who opens doorways.
notes: He can feel the presence of the far end of a door he has opened.
He does not know the exact range at which he can open a door relative to himself.
A normal, non-rage opening aimed at a visible point about twenty-five feet away, on a roll of 9, still produced an eighteen-foot door and landed short, over the lantern.
He can shut doors he has opened. Closing them while matter intersected the frame severed those branches.
He recalls Carlkin's instruction to practice the doors in the middle of a field, and agrees they should not be used in a crowded area or opened onto people.
personality: Treats the wind between two open doors as frightening and moves immediately to shut both.

notes: He refused to step through the new door until he had walked to the far end and checked for damage.
He theorizes that a stronger opening makes a larger door, that Gerk may need to remember a place fondly to arrive nearer to it, and that a recent visit may make a destination easier.
He called for Guidance on the line-of-sight attempt.
His lantern was pulled through the doors, rolled, and left dinged but intact. He recovered it.
He judges the cutting effect wildly dangerous and says they should not use it in a crowded area or carelessly teleport to people.
personality: Cautious about untested doorway effects and wants to evaluate a destination before using it.

Doorway.existing: A supernatural passage Gerk opens between locations.
notes: This opening was about eighteen feet tall and seven feet wide, notably larger than Gerk's usual doors. Whether size scales with how strongly he opens it is Sylan's theory, not a confirmed rule.
The same forest continued on the far side, about a quarter mile south. Gerk could feel that far end while the door remained open.
Branches occupying the doorway's space became semi-translucent while it was open. Closing it cleanly severed them, with no burn marks or residual debris, and the limbs fell.
Two doors left open at once pulled wind between them in a vacuum or vortex strong enough to suck a lantern from one door into the other. Shutting the doors stopped the wind.
A line-of-sight opening can miss: a normal opening aimed twenty-five feet away landed short, on the lantern.
Carlkin had told them to practice this in an open field. An earlier opening into the kitchen could have cut Mahali; a prior use involving the boat was described as ripping something out of reality.
openQuestions: What caused the initial disturbance of birds at the far door, which Sylan still could not explain after finding no crater?

notes: It was sitting near the point Gerk tried to open onto, past a crossing.
The vacuum between the two open doors sucked it through. It rolled and was left disheveled with a ding or two, but it was not shattered. Sylan gathered it.

Carlkin.existing: Turtle-like ally believed to be back in Langdale.
notes: Gerk recalls that Carlkin told them to practice opening these doors in the middle of a field.
